_: THE GEMINI DOM CONTRACT. Every value here was read off the live page, not
guessed - three separate outages in the prototype came from guessing.
This is the ONE file to edit when Gemini's UI changes; nothing outside
this directory contains a Gemini selector.
Selectors carry both English and Portuguese labels because the account
language changes the aria-labels, and an English-only stopButton made
completion detection fail silently on a pt-BR session.
_composer: A Quill editor, not a textarea, so setInputFiles/fill do not apply.
Two nodes match; the first is the live one. Wait for VISIBLE, not merely
present: a leftover file-viewer overlay leaves it attached but hidden,
and waiting on presence then hangs for the full timeout.
_sendButton: Enter does NOT submit on this build - verified directly. The button is
the only path, and it stays enabled throughout, so its state says
stopButton: button[aria-label*='Stop response' i], button[aria-label*='Stop' i], button[aria-label*='Parar' i]
_stopButton: Visible only while generating: the primary completion signal.
_copyButton: Returns Gemini's ORIGINAL MARKDOWN - pipe tables, intact LaTeX, fenced
code. innerText returns none of that. message-actions holds exactly
newChatButton: button[aria-label*='New chat' i], button[aria-label*='Nova conversa' i], a[aria-label*='New chat' i]

_export: MEASURED 2026-09-06 on a live thread. Gemini has no data-message-id: a
turn is a pair of custom elements, <user-query> and <model-response>, so
the ROLE is the element itself (roleMap) rather than an attribute.
Identity comes from the reply: <message-content id=
question carries no id of its own, so it borrows its reply's (pairId:
next) - stable across virtualization, and unlike hashing its text it does
not merge two identical questions into one.
The same r_... key also appears in response-container's jslog
BardVeMetadataKey, which is where to look if the id attribute ever moves.
The user's message contains an h5.cdk-visually-hidden reading 'You said',
so reading innerText on the container returned every question twice:
'You said X' + X. textExclude prunes it (on a clone - the live page is the
user's). The real text lives in .query-text > p.query-text-line.

modelPicker: button[aria-label*='mode picker' i], button[aria-label*='seletor de modo' i], button[aria-label*='mode selector' i], button[aria-label*='model' i]
_modelPicker: One control carries TWO dimensions: the model and the extended-thinking
toggle. Its aria-label reads 'Open mode picker, currently Flash' and
gains 'Extended' when thinking is on - that label is the only readable
confirmation of either setting, which is why provenance comes from here.
_models: Flash must not match Flash-Lite, hence the negative lookahead. Gemini
CAN sometimes switch model mid-thread, but unreliably and often only
after several turns - a Gemini-side bug - so each request opens a fresh
conversation and selects there, which is deterministic.
_upload: Uploads go through a CDP-dispatched (trusted) drag event. A synthetic
new DragEvent() is IGNORED - tested against document, window, body,
and main: zero attachments every time. There is no input[type=file] to
target, and the 'Upload & tools -> Files' menu opens an OS dialog and is
flaky, so it is only a fallback.
Readiness is uploader-file-preview appearing AND the uploading text
going away. Watching the send button instead never works: it is enabled
the whole time, so the prompt gets sent before the file has landed.
_sourceChip: sources-list is present in EVERY response, so including it made
browsed=true unconditionally. source-inline-chip is the real signal.
moreButton: message-actions button[aria-label*='More' i], message-actions button[data-test-id*='more' i]
_sources: Citations are exposed properly behind the message's '...' menu -> View
sources, which gives real URLs with text fragments. Scraping the body
chips alone misses them. The ignore list strips Google's own chrome
(account, policies, product pages) that shares the panel's markup.
_generatedFile: Gemini emits REAL files. The chip is <generated-file> with the true name
There is no <a download> and no blob: href anywhere, so a scan for
download affordances returns nothing - which is exactly how a real
generated CSV gets mistaken for 'just a code block'. 'Open' opens a
Drive-style viewer overlay IN THE SAME PAGE whose toolbar is
div[role=button] (Print / Download / More actions), NOT <button>, so
button[aria-label*=Download] only ever matches the code block's
'Download code'. Clicking div[aria-label=Download] fires a genuine
browser download. Verified end to end: 422 bytes of real CSV on disk.
toolMarker gates the whole lookup: .contains-extensions-response is
added only when the code/extension tool ran (checked across six output
types), so plain answers never wait for a file that cannot exist.
searchTransient: Searching the internet|Searching the web|Pesquisando na internet|Pesquisando
_transient: Placeholder text that appears BEFORE the answer. Treating it as the
answer returns 'Searching the internet' as the model's reply.
thinking-overlay is NOT a thinking indicator - it is present in every
response, so it cannot be used for this.
signedOutMarker: Faça login|Fazer login|Sign in to access|Sign in
accountMarker: a[aria-label*='Conta do Google' i], a[aria-label*='Google Account' i], img[alt*='@'], [data-test-id='account-menu-button']
challengeText: unusual traffic|tráfego incomum|verify you|not a robot

auth.accountMarker: a[aria-label*='Conta do Google' i], a[aria-label*='Google Account' i], img[alt*='@'], [data-test-id='account-menu-button']
auth.challengePattern: unusual traffic|tráfego incomum|verify you|not a robot

_auth: VERIFIED 2026-09-06 against this live signed-in profile: the cookie jar
held SID, __Secure-1PSID and __Secure-3PSID, and the pattern matched all
HOW SIGNED-IN IS PROVEN, strongest signal first. Google keeps no
same-origin session endpoint we can call, so the cookie jar is the
authority here: those names are httpOnly, which is exactly why
document.cookie cannot see them and the browser context must be asked
instead. The DOM markers below rank last - they are a guess about a
translated string, and this account renders in pt-BR.
RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-06: the live jar carries SID, __Secure-1PSID and
__Secure-3PSID (153 chars each), which is what authCookiePattern matches.
_signIn: A rendered composer does NOT mean signed in: an anonymous session shows
one too, and requests then run against no account. Sign-in must be
confirmed from a real account marker.
_attachStrategy: Synthetic DragEvents are ignored and there is no input[type=file]; CDP dispatches a trusted drag that takes file paths.
_pickerStrategy: One control carries model AND extended thinking; its aria-label is the only readable state for either.
errorText: Sorry, something went wrong|Something went wrong|Algo deu errado|Ocorreu um erro|try your request again
_errorText: Gemini renders its OWN failures as an ordinary assistant message, e.g.
'Sorry, something went wrong. Please try your request again.' Extraction
happily returns that as the model's answer - 59 chars, markdown=true,
indistinguishable from a real reply. In a batch that silently poisons rows.
Matching it turns the failure into a retryable error instead.

classify.match: excesso|limite de|too many|rate limit|slow down|tente novamente mais tarde|try again later

_notices: MEASURED 2026-09-06: a freshly loaded gemini.google.com has NO overlay
container at all - no .cdk-overlay-container, no [role=dialog], no
snackbar. Angular CDK IS in use (the transcript carries .cdk-visually-hidden
labels), so CDK's overlay container is where a notice will appear, but its
WORDING HAS NEVER BEEN OBSERVED and is not guessed here.
This spec is therefore STRUCTURAL: it has no `match`, so it reports any
visible overlay. `classify` gives kinds to text we can recognise; anything
else is reported as kind 'unknown', which is honest - a caller learns the
UI is blocked without being handed a category we invented.
SAFETY: because a structural spec matches ANY dialog - including one asking
whether to delete a conversation - a button is only clicked when its own
label matches dismissText exactly. Otherwise the only gesture used is
TO CALIBRATE PROPERLY: when Gemini next shows a notice, run
logs the full text it saw - then add a `match` and a measured kind here.
dismissText is anchored but tolerates surrounding whitespace: a button's
innerText carries padding, and a strictly anchored ^...$ matched nothing
- measured, the close button was found and then never clicked.
